subsystems.name: Quantum processor
subsystems.role: the hardware that performs quantum operations on qubits.
parts: qubits (superconducting, trapped ion, photonic, or other modalities)

subsystems.name: Control and readout electronics
subsystems.role: generates the precise pulses that manipulate qubits and reads out their final states.

subsystems.name: Quantum software stack
subsystems.role: translates a materials problem into a runnable quantum circuit and manages hardware noise.

subsystems.name: Quantum algorithms for materials
subsystems.role: methods that simulate electron behaviour to predict material properties.
parts: quantum machine learning for property prediction

subsystems.name: Classical computing infrastructure
subsystems.role: runs the hybrid loop, optimises parameters, and benchmarks quantum results.
parts: density functional theory and molecular dynamics codes

subsystems.name: Materials synthesis and characterisation
subsystems.role: tests quantum predictions in the real world and feeds results back.

buildSteps.title: Choose a target materials problem
buildSteps.detail: Pick a property to improve — for example, a catalyst that lowers activation energy or an electrolyte that conducts ions faster — and define it in computable terms.

buildSteps.title: Encode the electronic structure
buildSteps.detail: Write the Schrödinger equation for the relevant atoms and electrons as a Hamiltonian, often using a basis set that balances accuracy and qubit count.

buildSteps.title: Map the Hamiltonian to qubits
buildSteps.detail: Use fermion-to-qubit transformations such as Jordan–Wigner or Bravyi–Kitaev so the problem can be expressed as quantum gates.

buildSteps.title: Select a quantum algorithm
buildSteps.detail: For today's noisy hardware choose a shallow variational method like VQE; for future fault-tolerant machines plan for quantum phase estimation.

buildSteps.title: Compile and optimise the circuit
buildSteps.detail: Translate the algorithm into the native gates of the chosen quantum processor, minimising depth and two-qubit operations.

buildSteps.title: Apply error mitigation or correction
buildSteps.detail: Use techniques like zero-noise extrapolation or, eventually, full quantum error correction to reduce the impact of decoherence.

buildSteps.title: Execute on quantum hardware
buildSteps.detail: Run the circuit on a quantum processor, often in a loop with a classical optimiser that adjusts parameters.

buildSteps.title: Validate and feed back
buildSteps.detail: Compare results with classical simulations and, where possible, synthesise and measure the material to confirm or correct the prediction.

prerequisites.why: materials simulations need deep circuits, but today's qubits lose coherence long before such circuits finish.
current devices offer tens to a few hundred noisy qubits, far short of what realistic materials require.

prerequisites.tech: Quantum algorithms for chemistry and materials
prerequisites.why: small molecules have been simulated on quantum hardware, but complex solids and strongly correlated systems remain out of reach.
density functional theory and laboratory synthesis provide the benchmarks and feedback needed to trust quantum results.
cooling and addressing thousands of qubits without overwhelming heat load is an unsolved engineering problem.

pathway.milestone: proof-of-concept simulations of small molecules on noisy quantum computers
pathway.unlocks: early evidence that quantum hardware can reproduce known chemistry.

pathway.milestone: error mitigation and hybrid algorithms handle larger molecules and simple crystalline materials
pathway.unlocks: quantum-assisted screening of candidate compounds for batteries or catalysts.

pathway.milestone: early fault-tolerant devices demonstrate quantum advantage for a specific materials problem
pathway.unlocks: a credible reason for industry to invest in quantum materials design.

pathway.milestone: routine quantum-assisted design of catalysts, superconductors and battery materials
pathway.unlocks: faster discovery cycles for clean energy and advanced manufacturing.
